title: Day 760: Rocha Moya Requests Second Leave, Just 34 Hours After Resuming Governorship
detail: Rubén Rocha Moya filed a new leave-of-absence request with the Permanent Deputation of the Sinaloa Congress on Saturday, August 22, 2026 — only 34 hours after he had resumed his post following a 112-day absence on August 21. Unlike his first leave (a fixed period beginning May 1), the new request was for an indefinite period exceeding 30 days, with no set return date. The document was addressed to Juan Diego Aranzubia Iturrios, president of the Congress's Mesa Directiva. The renewed departure followed continued pressure from within his own Morena party — including from Senator Ricardo Monreal — and unresolved US Department of Justice drug-trafficking and weapons-trafficking accusations against him filed in the April 29–30 SDNY indictment. The Permanent Deputation convened to schedule an extraordinary session of the full Congress for Monday, August 24 to process the request and name a replacement.

media.caption: Rubén Rocha Moya's second leave-of-absence request reaches the Sinaloa Congress, August 22, 2026

title: Day 760: Federal Government Deploys 2,000 Additional Troops to Culiacán After Bloody Weekend
detail: The Mexican Army sent approximately 2,000 additional specialized personnel, trained for tactical operations in urban zones, into Culiacán on Saturday, August 22, 2026, coordinating with the National Guard to reinforce security after Friday's eight-victim homicide/femicide tally and the preceding week's Concordia/Culiacán/Mazatlán explosives and drug-lab seizures. The reinforcement adds to the roughly 13,300 federal troops already deployed statewide since late 2024. SEDENA, the National Guard, SSPC, the FGE, the Federal Public Ministry and SEMAR were all cited as coordinating agencies; no immediate operational results from the new deployment were reported.

media.caption: Mexican Army personnel arrive in Culiacán as part of a 2,000-troop security reinforcement, August 22, 2026
